terms.comment: Classically the Greek running track and the ground round it, where hominum cōpiae cum laxāmentō āthlētās certantēs spectāre could watch the athletes (Vitr. 5.11.4, as Morgan–Owens quotes it); also a measure of length, a stade.

terms.gloss: an arena, a large round stadium
terms.comment: The Roman arena, built all round for shows; a covered sports arena is amphitheātrum tēctum (Morgan–Owens).

terms.gloss: the arena, the sanded floor of an amphitheatre

phrases.english: as runners shout out on the track

sources: Lewis & Short: stadium · Lewis & Short: amphitheatrum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 45, 50, checked against the searchable text of the book on 11 November 2026.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. arena, stadium.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
